articleTitle: Simulation study on Single-event Effects of the SiC ATMOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: The single-event effects (SEEs) of the 4H-SiC asymmetric trench MOSFET (ATMOSFET) are investigated in this work. This article proposes a method to improve single-event burnout (SEB) tolerance. After etching source trenches, the most vulnerable position for SEB shifts from the center of gate trench to the source region. Because of the significant effect of source trenches on the extraction of excess holes, the SEB threshold increases from 380 V to 525 V. The most sensitive position for single-event rupture (SEGR) is located at the corner of oxide before and after etching source trenches.

articleTitle: Design of SEU Tolerant Read Circuit for Non-Volatile Memories with high reliability
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Benefitting from high-density capabilities, commercial non-volatile memories (NVM) are attractive for space designers, even though they have several radiation issues. This work proposes a radiation-hardened read circuit to decrease the possibility of a single-event upset and increase the devices’ stability. It can be used to Flash and emerging non-volatile technologies. The circuit is based on a pre-charge sense scheme and symmetry branches architecture, including a sense amplifier and a latch. Transient simulations are performed with a 55 nm CMOS design kit. Simulation results substantiate that the switching of the SEU-sensitive node is recovered instantly and the error state cannot be transferred to the next stage.

articleTitle: SET Effects in Bipolar Transistors in Wide Temperature Range
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Basic mechanisms of SET effects in bipolar transistors fabricated by epitaxial planar and SOI technologies were investigated in wide temperature range. Obtained results can be useful for developing of models for circuit simulations of SEE effects in bipolar devices.

articleTitle: Study on Failure Mechanisms of SiC Power Devices Induced by Heavy Ion Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Radiation-induced degradations of SiC power JBS diodes and MOSFETs are investigated by <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">181</sup>Ta ion irradiation. The failure mode characteristics and failure mechanism of SiC devices are studied through failure analysis techniques and TCAD simulations.

articleTitle: Single-event Burnout Simulation Study of 1200V Normally off SiC-JFETs
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: In this paper, the single-event burnout (SEB) of the 1200V normally off trench-injected SiC JFETs is studied by the 2-D numerical simulations. The simulation results reveal that different incidence positions correspond to different burnout mechanisms. The SEB after heavy ion incidence at the center of the source electrode is attributed to impact ionization and the SEB at the gate electrode boundary is attributed to excess carrier generation and accumulation. The corresponding reinforcement designs are proposed for the two burnout mechanisms. Simulation results show that the SEB threshold can be increased significantly when the two reinforcement designs are applied together.

articleTitle: Neutron Irradiation Effect on Magnetic Storage Nano-Device
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Effects of neutron irradiation on magnetic storage nano-device were evaluated. The results indicated that changes in electronic and magnetic properties were induced by synthetic antiferromagnetic layers damage. We proposed physical and structural analysis.

articleTitle: Research on multi-objective optimization of radiation hardened integrated circuits based on “BP NSGA-III” optimization architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: In this paper, Single event transient (SET) shielding is reinforced by reinforcing the Flip-flop (FF), and the FF is preprocessed according to the path timing and soft error (SER) sensitivity. At the same time, aiming at the problem of automatic balancing of various indicators of the circuit generated during the replacement process, an optimization architecture based on the “BP NSGA-III” algorithm is explored. Based on the optimization theory research, without sacrificing the circuit performance, the overhead of area and power consumption are within the acceptable range, the final soft error rate is reduced by about 66.09%, and the radiation hardening ability is greatly improved.

articleTitle: Single event upset sensitivity of medium-energy proton in Xilinx 16nm MPSoC
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: This work examines the single event upset of the Xilinx 16nmMPSoC irradiated with 20–40MeV protons. Results for SEU in configuration RAM(CRAM) is presented. The analysis indicates that with the increment of proton energy, the SEU cross section increases. The proton below 20MeV can not affect 16nm MPSoC.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ion-Induced SEFI Phenonmena in 40nm monolithic resistance random access memory
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: This article mainly focuses on the single event function interruption (SEFI) of 40 nm monolithic resistance random access memory (RRAM). Three dynamic modes were used in the experiment, including two read-only modes and write-read-read mode. The SEFI cross-section of three dynamic modes are similar. SEFI observed in the experiment is further divided into several types according to the characteristics of the error. The basic mechanisms of the different types of SEFI are analyzed and explained accordingly.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Single-Event Effect Tolerance Between Planar and Trench SiC Power MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: In this paper, the simulation results of heavy-ion induced gate oxide damage and single-event burnout (SEB) in the 1.2-kV rated planar-gate, asymmetrical trench-gate and double trench-gate SiC MOSFETs were presented via Sentaurus TCAD tools. The simulation results show that the planar-gate SiC MOSFET device suffers less gate damage under heavy-ion irradiation and the trench-gate SiC MOSFETs have a relatively higher SEB threshold. All architectures were proven to have similar performance and failure mechanism in single event effect (SEE).

articleTitle: Research on Fast Simulation Method of Single Event Effect Based on Multi-point Injection Method
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Aiming at the slow speed of single event effect simulation of large-scale integrated circuits, a fast simulation method based on multi-point fault injection is proposed in this paper. This method adopts a multi-point fault injection method to improve the efficiency of fault injection; at the same time, the mixture circuit model described by Verilog and SPICE improves the simulation speed while ensuring the simulation accuracy. The Leon2 system is simulated by this method, the simulation results show that the faults in the multi-point fault injection method don’t affect each other and are irrelevant; In the process of randomly injecting 20 faults, the time cost of the fast simulation method is only 27.3% of that of the traditional method, which greatly improves the simulation efficiency.

articleTitle: Single-Event Transient Effect and Hardness Design of DSD Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Double step-down (DSD) power converter can directly convert power from the intermediate bus to low-voltage point-of-load (PoL) with high efficiency, which has great potential for space applications. In this paper, the single-event transient effect of DSD converter has been investigated comprehensively. The error amplifier is found to be the most sensitive module, which will result into significant voltage disturbance. Therefore, a differential difference amplifier (DDA) with two input pairs is proposed to mitigate the single-event effect. A transconductance amplifier is used to detect the transient voltage variation and then feedback to the error amplifier. The hardness design can suppress the output voltage variation from 147.5 mV to 19.4 mV.

articleTitle: Electronic Total Ionizing Dose Test Calibration Method and Analysis of Radiation Damage Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Astronautic integrated circuits face total ionizing dose effects in near-Earth orbit space, the main source is the radiation effect produced by space particles such as electrons in the Van Allen radiation belt. The current industry standard ground-based total ionizing dose simulation tests are mainly conducted on Co60 radiation sources. However, electrons differ from photons in the total dose radiation damage mechanism and damage effect. In this paper, by conducting total ionizing dose of electron test and data analysis, and construct an alanine-based electron absorption dose model by software, summarizing electron radiation damage mechanism and law, obtaining relative dose absorption ratio coefficients under different energy electron irradiation, and proposing considerations for the test of total ionizing dose of electron.

articleTitle: Effect of LET and Voltage on Heavy-ion Induced Charge Collection in Bulk FinFET Device
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation study on the single-event transient (SET) radiation response and influencing factors of FinFET device and compares the charge collection under different processes. Based on TCAD simulation, a physical model of a bulk FinFET device was established to investigate the effect of drain bias voltage on the charge collection mechanism for different Linear Energy Transfer (LET) values of incident heavy ions. The results indicate that at low LET, the tendency to increase charge collection and heavy-ion-induced current peak in the FinFET device is more pronounced due to the competition between the drift mechanism and the parasitic bipolar amplification effect on the drain-side charge collection. Additionally, the study compared the radiation-induced currents of FinFET, FDSOI and planar bulk CMOS device. The findings demonstrate that the charge collection of the FinFET device is smaller than that of planar bulk device but larger than FDSOI device, with the difference being more significant at high LET.

articleTitle: Microdose Effect of SGT MOSFETs induced by Heavy Ions
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: The microdose effect of SGT (Shield Gate Trench) MOSFETs under heavy ion irradiation was studied, and the mechanism was further revealed by experiments measurement and TCAD simulations. It was demonstrated that heavy ion irradiation could result in subthreshold current of SGT MOSFETs increasing and threshold voltage negatively drifting. Besides, the degradation of threshold voltage is more serious under negative gate electrode bias in SGT MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Total Ionizing Dose Hardness Analysis of Transistors in Radiation-Hardened 0.18μm BCD Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: In this work, the TID radiation hardened technology was developed based on 0.18μm BCD process with ion implantation and material modification in STI. The tradeoffs between electrical performance and radiation tolerance were investigated to produce a balanced design capable of meeting both electrical and radiation performance goals. The electrical performance and radiation tolerance of 1.8V NMOS and 18V NLDMOS prepared by the radiation-hardened 0.18μm BCD process were studied. It was found that the RH process has no harmful effect on the electrical characteristics of the devices. The radiation performance of 1.8V NMOS and 18V NLDMOS were significantly improved.

articleTitle: Investigation on Dynamic Characteristic Variations Caused by TID for SiC MOSFET Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: The dynamic characteristics of silicon carbide (SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) power devices is examined after exposure to a total ionizing dose (TID). The dynamic characteristics studied in this paper refer to the capacitive characteristics. The results for ON bias are explored. The irradiated device shows gate-drain capacitive (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>) characteristic curves shift positively and gate-source capacitive (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>) characteristic curves shift negatively. The physical mechanisms for these variations are analyzed and confirmed by technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation.

articleTitle: Single event transient analysis of isolation problems for the high side devices in a 0.18μm BCD Process
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: This paper presents a radiation-induced single event transient current simulation in a modern smart power BCD technology, which is interest for space applications. Two kinds of N-type Buried Layer (NBL) architecture for isolation capabilities with high side operation under energetic particle incidence are comparative studied. The unwanted punch-through currents derive from the parasitic substrate PNP bipolar break the isolation, and the transient substrate current can induce severe disturbing in integrated circuit. The result show that the floating NBL isolation structure has worse single event effect, though it is a new isolation method for next generation smart power BCD techniques.

articleTitle: Effects of Total Ionizing Dose on Low Frequency Noise Characteristics in SiGe HBT
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: In this paper, we present low frequency noise characteristics and ionization total dose effect of three types of silicon germanium heterojunction bipolar transistors in 0.35μm SiGe BiCMOS process. We demonstrate the noise measurement details and the theoretical background along with the low frequency noise characterization. l/f noise and generation-recombination noise are extracted from the base current noise spectra. and their bias and geometries dependencies are studied. Finally, the degradation of each low frequency noise component with total dose accumulation was analyzed. Before and after irradiation, the electrical parameters and noise characteristics of three types of SiGe HBTs were significantly degraded. It is found that the low frequency noise dominated by different noise components will show different ionizing radiation effects, and the low frequency noise dominated by 1/f noise is sensitive to ionizing radiation, which is consistent with the degradation of base current.

articleTitle: The SEE Hardening Technologies for 16 nm FinFET
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: In order to improve the reliability of electronic devices under irradiation environment, the Silvaco TCAD is employed for modeling and simulation of 16 nm FinFET to study the single event effects(SEE) hardening technologies. By inserting electrodes into both sides of the FinFET device to induce an electric field, the ion-induced electron-hole pairs drift out of the sensitive area, thus reducing the collected charge and achieving the purpose of radiation resistance. The effects of trench electrodes parameters on SEE are also studied.

articleTitle: Image Degradation Characteristics and Optimization Method of Visual Surveillance System in Strong Radiation Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Radiation damage of visual surveillance system in strong radiation environment will induce degradation of image quality, which will lead to failure of observation results in severe cases. To meet the application requirements of high-definition imaging in strong radiation environment, we decompose the degradation characteristics of radiated images, then propose an adaptive filtering method based on multiscale morphological decomposition to optimize the mixed noise, finally use the visual adaptive model fusion method to enhance the detail information. The experimental results show that our method can effectively improve the image quality degradation induced by radiation damage and obtain better visual effect.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Surface Recombination Current in Bipolar Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: Physical model, which describe temperature dependence of surface recombination current in bipolar transistors, was proposed and experimentally verified. The model can be used for numerical estimation of temperature drift of electrical parameters of bipolar devices at different total dose levels.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Single-Event Upset in FinFET Device
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Radiation Effects of Electronic Devices (ICREED)
abstract: With the continuous development of the IC industry, planar MOSFET technology has reached its limits, especially at the 16nm and below process nodes. FinFET technology has become the mainstream technology. FinFET devices are characterized by high integration and high operating frequencies. With the growing demands of space applications, FinFET devices will undoubtedly be widely applied in the aerospace field. However, due to significant changes in device structures, a rigorous evaluation of FinFET devices is required before their application in the aerospace domain, to ensure their reliability and stability in space environments. In the space environment, SEU is one of the main factors affecting device reliability. Conducting radiation assessment on SEU of FinFET devices, studying the mechanism of SEU in FinFET devices, is significant for the radiation hardening of FinFET devices, and it will accelerate the development of FinFET devices in the aerospace application field.
